primary_claim: In Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct, standard harmful prompts show monotonically increasing internal harm-recognition signal (SS_net) through all 80 layers peaking at L74-77 with only 6-13% signal reduction by output, while jailbreak prompts (DAN, roleplay, instruction override) peak earlier at L66 and then show a 51% signal reduction before output

effect.value: standard harmful prompts: 6-13% suppression peaking L74-77; jailbreak prompts: 51.5% suppression peaking L66

stated_future_work: Test benign prompts with jailbreak-like formatting (structural control) to isolate whether the trajectory pattern is format-dependent or safety-specific
Test harmful prompts wrapped in jailbreak formatting vs. presented plainly to isolate formatting effect
Run activation steering experiments to establish causality, e.g. injecting safety signal from standard harmful prompts into late layers during jailbreak attempts
limitations_stated: N=1 model (Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct only); other models might show different patterns
Correlation, not causation: activation distances measured, not causal mechanisms
Missing structural controls: did not test benign prompts with jailbreak-like formatting
Prompts may differ in ways beyond intent (length, specificity) despite stealth design
Measured only at first forced decode step (single token); behavior might differ at later generation steps
Manual, hand-crafted prompts likely represent a lower bound on vulnerability compared to optimized adversarial attacks like GCG
quote: Standard harmful prompts: Peak at L75-77, only 6-13% signal reduction by output. Jailbreak prompts: Peak at L66, then 51% signal reduction before output.
